items.headline: Flood Warning issued October 1 at 10:27AM AKDT until October 3 at 7:45AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:

continue to drop into Friday. Levels on the Mendenhall are rising and
will continue through the release.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst continues.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the Mendenhall Glacier
Recreation area, View Drive and below Back Loop bridge.

* WHEN...Until 745 AM AKDT Saturday.

items.instruction:

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 1 at 7:27AM AKDT until October 1 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts near 40 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Municipality of Skagway.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
Strong winds could make docking high profile vessels difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds are expected Thursday
morning.
items.instruction: Winds this strong can make travel difficult. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 1 at 6:08AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
The latest camera imagery from inside the basin showed a drop in
water level with a corresponding rise in water levels on Mendenhall
Lake overnight. This could be an
indication that a basin release has started. NWS hydrologists and
meteorologists along with their partners are
assessing and analyzing the information.

Water levels in the basin are around 200 ft below where it was
before the release in August so if it is a release, the crest should
be much lower.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 1 at 5:03AM AKDT until October 1 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and 11
inches.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snowfall rates may be as high as 0.5"-1.0" per
hour Thursday morning. Most of the snowfall will be between MP 205
and MP 235 on the Richardson Highway.
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp; Eastern Alaska Range South of Trims Camp
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 30 at 7:58PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
With widespread colder weather across the Interior, another front
will bring light snow to portions of the area Wednesday night
through Thursday. Generally, around 1 to 3 inches are expected
around the Central & eastern Interior, generally from around the
Fairbanks Metro Area & eastward, although some isolated locations
could receive some locally marginally higher amounts, like toward
the Chena Recreational Area, Chena Hot Springs, the White
Mountains, & Fortymile Country. Take extra precautions
items.areas: Dalton Highway Summits; White Mountains and High Terrain South of the Yukon River; Fortymile Country; Upper Chena River Valley; Eielson AFB and Salcha; Chatanika River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 30 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Periods of snow continue through Friday night before gradually
drying on Saturday. Between Wednesday and Friday, snowfall totals
will range from 2 to 4 inches. Isolated locations under any
persistent heavier snow may see up to 6 inches.

Winds will be strongest today near Utqiagvik (Barrow) then weaken
tomorrow, but strongest Thursday night into Friday from Nuiqsut
to Kaktovik. Wind gusts will be up to 30 mph which may result in
areas of blowing/drifting snow, lowering visibility at times.
items.areas: Northern Arctic Coast; Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast
